places.name: Damascus
places.prompt: On the road to which city did a light from heaven shine round Saul?
places.text: And as he went on his journey, it came to pass that he drew nigh to Damascus; and suddenly a light from heaven shined round about him.
places.note: As Saul draws near Damascus on his journey, a light from heaven shines round about him.

places.name: Antioch
places.prompt: In which city were the disciples first called Christians?
places.text: And they conversed there in the church a whole year; and they taught a great multitude, so that at Antioch the disciples were first named Christians.
places.note: At Antioch the disciples are first named Christians.

places.name: Tarsus
places.prompt: In which Cilician city was Paul born?
places.text: And he saith: I am a Jew, born at Tarsus in Cilicia, but brought up in this city, at the feet of Gamaliel, taught according to the truth of the law of the fathers, zealous for the law, as also all you are this day:
places.note: Paul says he is a Jew, born at Tarsus in Cilicia.

places.name: Paphos
places.prompt: Which town on Cyprus did Paul and Barnabas reach after going through the whole island?
places.text: And when they had gone through the whole island, as far as Paphos, they found a certain man, a magician, a false prophet, a Jew, whose name was Bar-jesu:
places.note: Paul and Barnabas go through the whole island of Cyprus as far as Paphos.

places.name: Antioch in Pisidia
places.prompt: In which city of Pisidia did Paul and Barnabas enter the synagogue on the sabbath?
places.text: But they passing through Perge, came to Antioch in Pisidia: and entering into the synagogue on the sabbath day, they sat down.
places.note: Passing through Perge, they come to Antioch in Pisidia and enter the synagogue on the sabbath day.

places.name: Philippi
places.prompt: Which Roman colony, the chief city of part of Macedonia, did Paul and his companions visit?
places.text: And from thence to Philippi, which is the chief city of part of Macedonia, a colony. And we were in this city some days conferring together.
places.note: They come to Philippi, a Roman colony and the chief city of part of Macedonia, and stay there some days.

places.name: Thessalonica
places.prompt: After Amphipolis and Apollonia, which Macedonian city with a synagogue of the Jews did Paul reach?
places.text: And when they had passed through Amphipolis and Apollonia, they came to Thessalonica, where there was a synagogue of the Jews.
places.note: Passing through Amphipolis and Apollonia, they come to Thessalonica, where there is a synagogue of the Jews.

places.name: Athens
places.prompt: In which city did Paul stand in the midst of the Areopagus and speak to its men?
places.text: But Paul standing in the midst of the Areopagus, said: Ye men of Athens, I perceive that in all things you are too superstitious.
places.note: Paul stands in the midst of the Areopagus and addresses the men of Athens.

places.name: Corinth
places.prompt: To which city did Paul come after leaving Athens?
places.text: After these things, departing from Athens, he came to Corinth.
places.note: Departing from Athens, Paul comes to Corinth.

places.name: Ephesus
places.prompt: Which great city of Asia did Paul reach after passing through the upper regions?
places.text: And it came to pass, while Apollo was at Corinth, that Paul having passed through the upper coasts, came to Ephesus, and found certain disciples.
places.note: Paul passes through the upper regions and comes to Ephesus, where he finds certain disciples.

places.name: Miletus
places.prompt: From which port did Paul send to Ephesus for the elders of the church?
places.text: And sending from Miletus to Ephesus, he called the ancients of the church.
places.note: From Miletus, Paul sends to Ephesus and calls the elders of the church.

places.name: Malta
places.prompt: Which island did Paul reach after the shipwreck, where the people showed no small courtesy?
places.text: And when we had escaped, then we knew that the island was called Melita. But the barbarians shewed us no small courtesy.
places.note: After the shipwreck they learn that the island is called Melita, and the people show them no small courtesy.
places.caveat: Melita is traditionally identified with Malta.

places.name: Syracuse
places.prompt: In which Sicilian city did Paul's ship stay three days on the way to Rome?
places.text: And when we were come to Syracusa, we tarried there three days.
places.note: They come to Syracuse and stay there three days.

places.name: Rome
places.prompt: Which city did Paul reach at the end of his journey as a prisoner?
places.text: Where, finding brethren, we were desired to tarry with them seven days: and so we went to Rome.
places.note: Finding brethren who ask them to stay seven days, they go on to Rome.

places.name: Patmos
places.prompt: On which island was John when he received the Apocalypse?
places.text: I John, your brother and your partner in tribulation, and in the kingdom, and patience in Christ Jesus, was in the island, which is called Patmos, for the word of God, and for the testimony of Jesus.
places.note: John writes that he was on the island called Patmos for the word of God and the testimony of Jesus.

places.name: Smyrna
places.prompt: Where was the church of Smyrna, one of the seven churches addressed in the Apocalypse?
places.text: And to the angel of the church of Smyrna write: These things saith the First and the Last, who was dead, and is alive:
places.note: The Lord tells John to write to the angel of the church of Smyrna.

places.name: Pergamum
places.prompt: Where was the church of Pergamum, one of the seven churches addressed in the Apocalypse?
places.text: And to the angel of the church of Pergamus write: These things, saith he, that hath the sharp two edged sword:
places.note: The Lord tells John to write to the angel of the church of Pergamum.

places.name: Thyatira
places.prompt: Where was the church of Thyatira, one of the seven churches addressed in the Apocalypse?
places.text: And to the angel of the church of Thyatira write: These things saith the Son of God, who hath his eyes like to a flame of fire, and his feet like to fine brass.
places.note: The Lord tells John to write to the angel of the church of Thyatira.

places.name: Sardis
places.prompt: Where was the church of Sardis, one of the seven churches addressed in the Apocalypse?
places.text: And to the angel of the church of Sardis, write: These things saith he, that hath the seven spirits of God, and the seven stars: I know thy works, that thou hast the name of being alive: and thou art dead.
places.note: The Lord tells John to write to the angel of the church of Sardis.

places.name: Philadelphia
places.prompt: Where was the church of Philadelphia, one of the seven churches addressed in the Apocalypse?
places.text: And to the angel of the church of Philadelphia, write: These things saith the Holy One and the true one, he that hath the key of David; he that openeth, and no man shutteth; shutteth, and no man openeth:
places.note: The Lord tells John to write to the angel of the church of Philadelphia.

places.name: Laodicea
places.prompt: Where was the church of Laodicea, one of the seven churches addressed in the Apocalypse?
places.text: And to the angel of the church of Laodicea, write: These things saith the Amen, the faithful and true witness, who is the beginning of the creation of God:
places.note: The Lord tells John to write to the angel of the church of Laodicea.

places.name: Crete
places.prompt: On which island did Paul leave Titus to set the church in order?
places.text: For this cause I left thee in Crete, that thou shouldest set in order the things that are wanting, and shouldest ordain priests in every city, as I also appointed thee:
places.note: Paul left Titus in Crete to set in order what was wanting and to ordain priests in every city.

places.name: Alexandria
places.prompt: Which great Egyptian city was the home of Apollos, an eloquent man mighty in the scriptures?
places.text: Now a certain Jew, named Apollo, born at Alexandria, an eloquent man, came to Ephesus, one mighty in the scriptures.
places.note: Apollos, an eloquent man mighty in the scriptures, was born at Alexandria.
places.caveat: Church tradition holds that the evangelist Mark founded the church of Alexandria.

places.name: Rome, St. Peter's Basilica
places.prompt: Where does tradition say the apostle Peter was martyred and buried?
places.text: Amen, amen I say to thee, when thou wast younger, thou didst gird thyself, and didst walk where thou wouldst. But when thou shalt be old, thou shalt stretch forth thy hands, and another shall gird thee, and lead thee whither thou wouldst not. And this he said, signifying by what death he should glorify God. And when he had said this, he saith to him: Follow me.
places.note: Jesus foretells that when Peter is old another will lead him where he would not go, signifying by what death he would glorify God.
places.caveat: According to Christian tradition Peter was crucified in Rome under Nero, and Catholic tradition holds that St. Peter's Basilica is his burial site.

places.name: Rome, Tre Fontane
places.prompt: Where does tradition say the apostle Paul was beheaded under Nero?
places.text: For I am even now ready to be sacrificed: and the time of my dissolution is at hand. I have fought a good fight, I have finished my course, I have kept the faith.
places.note: Paul writes that he is ready to be sacrificed, that he has fought a good fight, finished his course and kept the faith.
places.caveat: The Abbey of the Three Fountains was raised on the spot where, by tradition, Paul was beheaded by order of Nero.

places.name: Patras
places.prompt: Where does Christian tradition place the martyrdom of the apostle Andrew?
places.text: And Andrew, the brother of Simon Peter, was one of the two who had heard of John, and followed him.
places.note: Andrew, the brother of Simon Peter, is one of the two who hear John and follow.
places.caveat: According to Christian tradition, Patras is the place of Saint Andrew's martyrdom.

places.name: Hierapolis
places.prompt: In which city of Phrygia is the apostle Philip said to have spent his last years?
places.text: On the following day, he would go forth into Galilee, and he findeth Philip. And Jesus saith to him: Follow me.
places.note: Jesus finds Philip and says to him: Follow me.
places.caveat: The apostle Philip is said to have spent the last years of his life at Hierapolis.

places.name: Salamis
places.prompt: Where on Cyprus did Barnabas and Saul first preach in the synagogues of the Jews?
places.text: And when they were come to Salamina, they preached the word of God in the synagogues of the Jews. And they had John also in the ministry.
places.note: Coming to Salamis, they preach the word of God in the synagogues of the Jews, with John in the ministry.
places.caveat: Christian tradition holds that Barnabas was martyred at Salamis.

places.name: Caesarea
places.prompt: In which coastal city did the centurion Cornelius live?
places.text: And there was a certain man in Caesarea, named Cornelius, a centurion of that which is called the Italian band;
places.note: In Caesarea there is a man named Cornelius, a centurion of the Italian band.

places.name: Jerusalem
places.prompt: In which city were Paul and Barnabas received by the church, the apostles and the elders?
places.text: And when they were come to Jerusalem, they were received by the church, and by the apostles and ancients, declaring how great things God had done with them.
places.note: At Jerusalem they are received by the church, the apostles and the elders, and tell how great things God had done with them.

places.name: Joppa
places.prompt: In which port city did the disciple Tabitha, also called Dorcas, live?
places.text: And in Joppe there was a certain disciple named Tabitha, which by interpretation is called Dorcas. This woman was full of good works and almsdeeds which she did.
places.note: At Joppa there is a disciple named Tabitha, who is also called Dorcas and is full of good works and acts of charity.
places.caveat: Joppa is today Jaffa, the old port of Tel Aviv-Yafo.

places.name: Nicaea
places.prompt: Where was the first ecumenical council held, in 325?
places.text: Following this apostolic tradition, the Church confessed at the first ecumenical council at Nicaea (325) that the Son is "consubstantial" with the Father, that is, one only God with him.
places.note: The first ecumenical council confesses that the Son is consubstantial with the Father.

places.name: Constantinople
places.prompt: Where was the second ecumenical council held, in 381?
places.text: The second ecumenical council, held at Constantinople in 381, kept this expression in its formulation of the Nicene Creed and confessed "the only-begotten Son of God, eternally begotten of the Father, light from light, true God from true God, begotten not made, consubstantial with the Father".
places.note: The second ecumenical council keeps the expression "consubstantial" in its formulation of the Nicene Creed.

places.name: Ephesus
places.prompt: Where was the third ecumenical council held, in 431?
places.text: Opposing this heresy, St. Cyril of Alexandria and the third ecumenical council, at Ephesus in 431, confessed "that the Word, uniting to himself in his person the flesh animated by a rational soul, became man."
places.note: St. Cyril of Alexandria and the third ecumenical council confess that the Word became man.
